done.why: I ran out of turns while lost in the coal mine maze. I was holding the sapphire bracelet and still trying to reach the ladder. My last score check said 225 of 350.

about: This is a treasure hunt under and around a white house. You find valuables all over a large underground empire and carry them back to a trophy case that "expects to be filled." Most of the game is logistics: how much you can carry, which routes only go one way, and how to get your loot back up to the surface. This version adds a chimney that fits you, your lamp and one other thing. The trap door gets barred behind you. Some passages in the Round Room are blocked by cave-ins, so the routes aren't the ones I expected.

moments.note: The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it. I was cut off from the house right away.
Two hits with the sword killed the troll, and the score jumped to 35.
The Round Room says several passages are blocked by cave-ins, so the map isn't what I expected.
I sent a batch of compass directions without noticing I was in the Loud Room. All I got back was echoes.
Saying 'echo' changed the acoustics and let me take the platinum bar.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' Carrying limits kept me shuffling items back and forth.
West from the Dam went to Reservoir South, not back to the Deep Canyon. Later I walked a loop the wrong way because of it.
The chimney only fits you, your lamp and one thing more, so it becomes a one-treasure-per-trip elevator. A clever squeeze.
The thief wandered through the Studio and found nothing of value, even though the platinum bar was on the floor. Lucky.
Praying at the altar sent me straight to the forest with my treasures. A great shortcut back to the house.
The bell, candles and book ritual at the gates of Hades played out dramatically and the spirits fled.
Waving the sceptre made the rainbow solid, with a joke about the stairs and bannister, and a pot of gold appeared.
'You already have that!' I'd been carrying the switched-off lantern the whole time and thought I'd left it behind.
The coal mine is a maze of identical 'nondescript' rooms. I lost track fast and burned my last turns mapping it.

wished: I wished the score command didn't cost a move, or that I could see turns remaining. The 400-turn cap surprised me right in the middle of the maze.
I wanted to carry more than one treasure up the chimney, or to unbar the trap door from below.
I wanted a way through the coal mine that wasn't pure trial and error. Every room reads 'nondescript part of a coal mine'.
I never got to use the boat and pump on the river, or go after the thief for his loot.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: This line from the trophy case's description told me what the game wanted from me: fill the case.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: It made the underground feel like a trap, and every trip out turned into a puzzle.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: This one rule shaped my whole plan for getting treasures home.

lines.line: "Begone, fiends!" A heart-stopping scream fills the cavern, and the spirits, sensing a greater power, flee through the walls.
lines.why: The payoff for the Hades ritual, and the most dramatic moment I had.

lines.line: Suddenly, the rainbow appears to become solid and, I venture, walkable (I think the giveaway was the stairs and bannister).
lines.why: A funny line, and it unlocked the pot of gold and the beach beyond.

fun.why: There was a steady flow of treasure and puzzle payoffs: the troll, the echo, the rainbow, Hades, the coffin. Praying to get out of the temple felt great. Points come off for the coal mine slog at the end.

engagement.why: Having a clear goal (fill the case, push the score up) kept me planning routes the whole time. The score kept climbing: 35, 65, 130, 173, 209, 225.

difficulty.why: Most puzzles could be solved from what the text said. Weight limits, the chimney rule and the barred trap door made the logistics hard in a fair way. The maze and the turn cap were the only parts that felt harsh.

interestingness.why: The changes to the map made me pay attention: cave-ins in the Round Room, the Dam's west exit going to Reservoir South, the one-thing chimney. Twisting passages that loop between mirror rooms kept me guessing.

prose.why: The room text is vivid and dryly funny: the trophy case's 'patient air', the rainbow joke, the Hades sequence. The coal mine's repeated 'nondescript' rooms are deliberately flat.
